clue.text: Special effect on stage does for grand army (12, two words, apostrophe)

parts.note: to do for someone is to finish them off, and to pepper is to pelt with shot
a host is an army, as in the heavenly host

explanation.surface: A stage trick is said to wipe out a whole grand army.
explanation.walkthrough: PEPPER'S GHOST is a Victorian theatre illusion in which an angled sheet of glass makes a ghostly figure appear on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The illusion, named after John Henry Pepper, is a classic piece of theatrical trickery using reflected light.

clue.text: Corpuscle I damaged with TB — NHS is part of it (12, two words)

indicators.note: damaged signals that the letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A damaged blood cell and tuberculosis call to mind the National Health Service.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's state-funded National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: The state-run health service is one of the bodies owned and funded by government.

clue.text: Bit of money overseas I invested in superb piece of art

indicators.note: invested means put inside, as money goes into a fund

parts.note: posh means smart or first-rate
taken as written

indicators.note: just a piece, the first letter, of the word art

parts.note: the first letter stands for the whole word

explanation.surface: Some foreign cash is invested in a superb work of art.
explanation.definitionFit: The poisha is a small coin of Bangladesh, a hundredth of a taka.

clue.text: Conifers planted in coppice annually

indicators.note: the trees are planted in the following words, sitting within their letters

parts.note: the conifer genus runs across the two words, from the end of coppice into annually

explanation.surface: Fir trees are planted every year in a woodland copse.
explanation.walkthrough: A coppice is woodland regularly cut back to stumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Picea is the botanical genus of spruces, evergreen cone-bearing trees.

clue.text: Small stream runs poorly

parts.note: ill and poorly both mean unwell

explanation.surface: A little stream flows feebly.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A rill is a tiny brook or rivulet.

clue.text: The Family Tree, a play of Mamet's

indicators.note: a play on the letters, as in wordplay, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The Family Tree is offered as the title of a David Mamet drama.
explanation.walkthrough: David Mamet is an American playwright; 'play' sounds like his stage work.
explanation.definitionFit: A stemma is a genealogical pedigree, the chart of a line of descent.

clue.text: Will S's bride reared oriental shrub

indicators.note: reared means raised up, which in a down entry reads the name from bottom to top

parts.note: Shakespeare married Anne Hathaway, so her first name and initial

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's wife grew an eastern bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a shrub of Asia and North Africa whose leaves make a reddish dye.

clue.text: Set this loaded with small stone? Great stones!

indicators.note: to set type or a table is to arrange it, so the letters of the fruit are put in a new order to give this answer

parts.note: an orange is a fruit full of pips, the small stones of the question

explanation.surface: A weapon is loaded with a small stone, but a great one is called for.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse twist: rearranging the answer gives the pip-filled fruit. The onager was a Roman siege catapult that hurled great stones.
explanation.definitionFit: The onager was an ancient military engine built to throw heavy rocks at fortifications, so great stones were its ammunition.

clue.text: Air hostess in fancy lace brought over complimentary sweets etc (12, two words)

parts.note: trolley is a lace whose pattern is outlined in thicker thread
in Anglo-Indian use a dolly is a gift of fruit, sweets or flowers offered to a visitor

explanation.surface: A flight attendant in lacy finery hands round free snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: The air hostess really does bring complimentary snacks, but here those words define the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Trolley dolly is slang for a female flight attendant, who pushes the drinks cart along the aisle.

clue.text: Anterior insect parts are mostly on top when flying

indicators.note: flying letters scatter, so they land in a new arrangement
most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An insect's front parts sit mostly on top while it flies.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronotum is the upper plate of an insect's first thoracic segment, at the front of the body.

clue.text: Frolicsome nurse in pool

indicators.note: the nurse is placed inside the word for pool

parts.note: a kitty is a pool of money that players or contributors share

explanation.surface: A playful nurse splashes about in a swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: The pool is a fund of money, not water; EN is an Enrolled Nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitteny means playful like a young cat, a Chambers synonym of kittenish.

clue.text: Tit and sandpiper (female), common feature in plantations (7, two words)

parts.note: tit is a word for a teat or nipple
a ree is the female of the ruff, a sandpiper

explanation.surface: A tit and a female sandpiper are common birds of plantations.
explanation.walkthrough: Tit wants to be the bird alongside the sandpiper; it is the teat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea bushes are grown in rows on tea estates; the plant is called a tea tree.

clue.text: Recovering quickly from British form of E. coli

indicators.note: a form of something is a version of it, so the letters of the bacterium's name are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, its five letters reworked

explanation.surface: Someone bounces back from a British strain of a gut bacterium.
explanation.walkthrough: BR is the standard abbreviation for British. A bricole is a rebound, as of a ball off a wall or cushion.
explanation.definitionFit: A bricole is a rebounding stroke, and a rebound is a quick recovery, as in bouncing straight back.

clue.text: Country missing in dispersed defensive alliance

indicators.note: missing means the letters of in are left out of the word for country
dispersed says the two letters of in are scattered, not side by side, in the longer word

parts.note: a nation is a country
the word in is taken out letter by letter, its I and its N coming from separate places

explanation.surface: A country is absent from a scattered military alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization is a mutual-defence pact between Western states.

clue.text: Rascal nearly having wings clipped

indicators.note: clipping a bird's wings trims both sides, so the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: closely, as in closely resembling, means nearly

explanation.surface: A rogue very nearly gets grounded by having his wings clipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Losel is an old word for a worthless scoundrel or good-for-nothing.

clue.text: Boy meets girl: the result is a blazing affair

parts.note: a boy grows into a man, and man is used for any male
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A romance sparks between a boy and a girl and becomes a passionate affair.
explanation.walkthrough: The blazing affair sounds like a hot romance; it is a literal burner.
explanation.definitionFit: A mangal is a Middle Eastern charcoal brazier, an object in which fuel burns.

clue.text: He's nautical? As playing with this rope, etc?

indicators.note: playing with letters means moving them around, so the fodder is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor is described as nautical, with a rope and other gear.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of HE'S NAUTICAL are those of the answer plus AS and ETC, so remove those and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhaul is a nautical line used for hauling in a sail or spar, a type of rope.

clue.text: Maybe mature group upset when disheartened

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters of group are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: without its heart, the word loses its middle letters

parts.note: only the outside letters of when survive

explanation.surface: A mature group is upset when it loses heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Upgrown means fully grown, adult, which is one form maturity takes.

clue.text: Rare plant to procure as stuffing for cooked meat?

indicators.note: the procuring word is stuffed inside the meat

parts.note: veal is calf meat, the kind stuffed and roasted
to get is to procure

explanation.surface: A rare plant is fetched to stuff some roast meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rare' does not mean scarce: it marks the noun sense as rarely used.
explanation.definitionFit: Vegetal is mainly an adjective; as a noun meaning a vegetable or plant it is rare.

clue.text: Cable securing pet?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: short for coaxial cable, as used for TV aerials
second meaning: to win over or get by gentle fondling, as you would a pet

explanation.walkthrough: Chambers defines the verb as to persuade by fondling or flattery, which the question mark plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Coax is both electronics shorthand for a shielded wire and a verb for gently persuading.

clue.text: Lively female bird, it's often seen in orchards

parts.note: peart is a dialect word meaning lively or brisk
a ree, or reeve, is the female of the ruff, a wading bird

explanation.surface: A lively hen bird is a familiar sight in orchards.
explanation.definitionFit: Pears are a staple fruit crop, so the trees bearing them grow in many orchards.

clue.text: Vagrant scrambled last egg going round run

indicators.note: the mixed letters go round the abbreviation for run
scrambled, as with eggs, means the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, then mixed

explanation.surface: A tramp scrambles the last egg and then goes for a run.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run.
explanation.definitionFit: To straggle is to wander or stray from the route, the same roaming sense as vagrant.

clue.text: It doesn't produce much of a glow — try mixing with ale

definitions.text: It doesn't produce much of a glow

indicators.note: mixing the two words stirs their letters together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drink that leaves little glow is tried mixed with ale.
explanation.definitionFit: A raylet is a small beam of light, so it gives off only a faint gleam.

clue.text: Setter, maybe: 'Good solving (albeit old-fashioned) — drop in' (6, two words)

indicators.note: drop means the little word in is let fall from the longer one

parts.note: undoing once meant solving a riddle, a sense now archaic
taken as written

explanation.surface: The crossword setter wishes us good solving, old-fashioned though it is, and invites us to drop in.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter is a breed trained to point out game for shooters, one kind of gun dog.

clue.text: Like stuffing, good stuffing e.g.?

indicators.note: the second stuffing tells us good is stuffed inside the word for e.g.

parts.note: say, as in 'take, say, apples', introduces an example just like e.g.

explanation.surface: Something resembles stuffing, perhaps a good stuffing for example.
explanation.walkthrough: Sage and onion is the classic British stuffing for roast poultry, so a herby stuffing is sagy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagy means flavoured with or tasting of sage, the herb that seasons traditional stuffing.

clue.text: Antique copper colour? Wow, that's old!

parts.note: the as was a copper coin of ancient Rome
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: An antique copper colour is admired as a striking old shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's old' marks the definition as archaic: astone is a former verb for astonish.
explanation.definitionFit: To wow someone is to amaze them, which the obsolete astone also meant.

clue.text: Stylishness? Only moderate clothing line

indicators.note: clothing means dressing, so the moderate word wraps round the line

parts.note: fair means middling or only moderately good

explanation.surface: A line of clothing shows only moderate style.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the usual abbreviation for line.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair is a natural elegance or panache, close to stylishness.

clue.text: German river, dry at edges, put through sifting process

indicators.note: the word for dry is placed at both edges, round the river

parts.note: to ted is to spread out mown hay so it dries
the Ems flows through north-west Germany to the North Sea

explanation.surface: A German river, dried out at its banks, is passed through a sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: A temse is a sieve, so temsed means sifted, an old dialect verb.

clue.text: Small quantity MO cut up, mouldy

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the remainder is read from bottom to top
the letters of MO are cut away from the word for a small quantity

parts.note: a modicum is a small amount
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tiny portion of something was cut up and has gone mouldy.
explanation.walkthrough: MO looks like an abbreviation to expand, but its two letters are simply removed from the word for a small quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Mucid means musty or slimy with mould, from the Latin for mucus.

clue.text: Coley processed by Norway 'changed' island

indicators.note: processed, as fish are at a factory, means the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Coley fish are processed by Norway on some island.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the international vehicle code for Norway. 'Changed' because the island has since been renamed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceylon was renamed Sri Lanka in 1972, so it is an island whose name has changed.

clue.text: 'How are you?' 'Unco ——, hooey! Nae sae weel'

definitions.meaning: a Scots reply to a greeting with a gap after unco, the Scots word for very
the speaker goes on to say they are not so well, so the missing word means worse

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank clue in broad Scots: waur is Scots for worse, so the reply reads 'very much worse, not so well'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect waur is the comparative of bad, the equivalent of English worse.

clue.text: Connect with Cupid

definitions.meaning: first meaning, as two words: to put a horse to a cart is to hitch it up
second meaning: a chubby winged child in Renaissance art, often Cupid

explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words, the answer is the phrase for harnessing; as one word it is the painted cherub.
explanation.definitionFit: Putti are the naked winged infants of Italian painting, frequently representing the love god.

clue.text: Weight? Plenty cutting back

indicators.note: cutting back here means turning back, so the phrase for plenty is read in reverse

parts.note: a lot means plenty

explanation.surface: Someone with plenty of weight is cutting back.
explanation.definitionFit: The tola is an Indian unit of mass, about eleven and a half grams, used for gold.

clue.text: A lady misbehaving in company? The opposite — upper stratum

indicators.note: the surface puts the lady in company; the parse needs it the other way round
the opposite of the stated order, so company goes inside rather than outside
misbehaving suggests the letters of a lady are disorderly

parts.note: taken as written, then mixed

explanation.surface: A lady behaves badly at a social gathering among the upper class.
explanation.walkthrough: CO is the usual abbreviation for company. Day-coal is the mining term for coal lying nearest the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Day-coal is the top seam of coal in a mine, the one nearest daylight.

clue.text: With claret-vessels aplenty Earl opens wine before us

indicators.note: the earl's letter goes into the opening part of the word for wine

parts.note: vino is informal for wine
taken as written

explanation.surface: An earl opens a bottle of wine for us, with plenty of claret on hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Claret is old slang for blood, so claret-vessels are veins.
explanation.definitionFit: Veinous means having many prominent veins, the blood channels that claret refers to.

clue.text: Historical rally round old St Petersburg, leaderless, making matters worse?

indicators.note: the old word for rally goes round the trimmed city name

parts.note: rely is an obsolete form of rally, to bring together again

indicators.note: the city name loses its leading letter

parts.note: St Petersburg was called Petrograd from 1914 to 1924

explanation.surface: A historical rally round old St Petersburg, without its leader, only made things worse.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrogradely means backwards or towards a worse state, the way matters deteriorate.
